Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
Text
We believe that all children have the right to a broad, balanced, relevant and differentiated curriculum that is appropriate to their levels of ability. The curriculum is flexible and will be adapted and differentiated where necessary to meet the needs of the individual child.
We adhere to three key principles for inclusion:
setting suitable learning challenges
responding to all pupils' diverse needs
overcoming potential barriers to learning and assessment for individuals and groups of individuals
We recognise that all children are unique and learn at different rates. Many factors affect attainment, progress and overall achievement but a child with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) will need support that is ‘in addition to or different from’ the other children in his / her year group. This additional support for children may require short or long term interventions recognising single or a combination of areas of needs.

Pupil Premium
Text
At Hiltingbury Infant school, we are committed to ensuring that every child has the opportunity to achieve their full potential, regardless of their background or circumstances. We use Pupil Premium funding to provide targeted support, high-quality teaching, and enriching experiences that help pupils overcome barriers to learning and make the very best progress.
Our approach focuses on:
High-quality teaching for all pupils.
Targeted academic support where needed.
Enhancing children's wellbeing, attendance and engagement in school life.
Providing wider opportunities and experiences that support personal development.
Ensuring that all pupils feel included, valued and successful.
We carefully monitor the impact of our spending to ensure that funding is used effectively and delivers positive outcomes for pupils.
Information about how our Pupil Premium funding is allocated, the barriers to learning faced by eligible pupils, and the impact of previous spending can be found in our Pupil Premium Strategy Statement below.

Starting School
Text
Hiltingbury Infants' is an outstanding school where children thrive through our broad and balanced curriculum, learner for life skills and shared vision of 'learning, caring and achieving together'.
Please find some important information below that will help to support the transition into school for your child.
Home visits will take place between 3rd and 7th September and a time will have been provided to you at one of the settling in sessions in July. If you have not received a time for your visit please contact the school office.
Tuesday 8th September - Your child will attend school for half a day. Children born between September and February will attend the morning session from 8.45am to 11.45am and children born between March and August will attend the afternoon session from 12.10pm to 15.10pm.
Wednesday 9th September – from this date there is the option for your child to start full time. We recognise that for some children a part-time option may suit your child’s needs better. We can personalise this to suit your child's/family needs which can be discussed at home visits. From Monday 21st September we expect all children to be full time.

Uniform
Text
The uniform at Hiltingbury Infant School is grey trousers, skirt or pinafore. This should be worn with a navy sweatshirt and a white polo shirt, both of which are available with the school logo.
In summer, blue and white dresses or shorts may be worn.
We ask that children wear appropriate footwear in black or navy for school. Children need a coat in cooler weather as they have daily outdoor play.
It is important that children are properly dressed for physical education. For PE days, navy or black shorts and a white T-Shirt should be worn (Logo options are available but not required).
PLEASE ENSURE THAT ALL CLOTHING IS NAMED, including socks, shoes and bags.
Logo uniform can be purchased via Koolskools.
You can also purchase secondhand uniform via the HSPTA website.
No jewellery is to be worn or brought into school unless this is for religious reasons, and has been discussed with the class teacher. Studs may be worn in pierced ears, but not on PE days. Children have to be able to remove the studs themselves, as teachers are not allowed to do this. No earrings may be worn during any PE lessons, due to health and safety reasons and in conjunction with county guidelines.
We ask that children with long hair have this tied back securely on PE days for safety reasons.
